item.title: Why I moved this site off Docsify and onto Hugo
item.description:
This site used to run on Docsify — markdown rendered client-side by JS, no build step. Fine for a quick personal page, bad for anything you want search engines to actually read: crawlers that don’t execute JS see an empty shell, and there’s no per-page metadata to speak of.

I wanted something boring instead: static HTML generated at build time, no framework churn, no dependency on a CDN script staying online. Hugo fit — a single binary, no Ruby/Node toolchain to maintain, markdown in, HTML out. I build locally and push the output straight to /docs; no CI pipeline to babysit.

item.title: Cutting feature delivery from two weeks to three days with AI-assisted development
item.description:
Rolling out AI-assisted development across a 9-person cross-functional team wasn’t about handing everyone a Copilot license and calling it done — most of the gain came from where in the workflow we applied it.

Scaffolding, not judgment. The time savings showed up in boilerplate-heavy work — API endpoint scaffolding, migration files, repetitive test setup, translating a spec into a first-pass implementation. Architecture decisions, service boundaries, and anything touching regulatory logic stayed human-reviewed line by line. The tool is fast at typing; it’s not accountable for a compliance requirement being met.

item.title: ERC-4626 vaults for RWA: what changes when the collateral isn't crypto
item.description:
ERC-4626 was designed for yield-bearing crypto vaults — deposit an ERC-20, get shares, redeem later at a different exchange rate. The mechanics translate reasonably well to tokenized real-world assets, but a few assumptions in the standard stop holding once the underlying isn’t sitting on-chain.

Redemption isn’t instant. A crypto vault can settle a withdrawal in the same block. An RWA vault backed by a bond or a fund unit is gated by the actual settlement cycle of that asset — T+2, a subscription/redemption window, sometimes a manual custodian step. previewRedeem and maxWithdraw need to reflect that reality rather than assume liquidity is always there, or integrators will build against numbers the vault can’t honor.
